title: Catch up on TCA + Native Dispatch

tldr: The FedEx account work is split into MVP1 (CSV upload from Dispatch Cloud format) and MVP2 (API). The team wants to prove the CSV route works with a swap-out of the new system before the 11:30 call with Pete.
The new system was demoed: CSV upload with configurable column mapping, drag and drop, label preview and save, bulk print, packaging presets and unit conversion, and a spec test customer.
The plan is to test against the live TCA FedEx endpoint with a smoke-test order, which Speaker 1 will delete immediately because it is bill on scan.
The open issue for Pete is how to position the API: as a stopgap, not Merrick, while the Americans expect an API in about two weeks.
A mock of every carrier proxy was shown as a possible test playground, along with a side topic on the mezzanine PDA rebuild.
decisions: Treat SFTP as out of scope for now and use drag and drop CSV upload for the first test.
Run a test of the CSV flow against the live TCA endpoint this morning, before the 11:30 call with Pete.
Position the new system to the Americans and Pete as a stopgap or stepping stone, not Merrick, with the API to follow later.
Keep the carriers team out of this work, since too many people are getting involved.

actions.text: Send the TCA FedEx account info and the endpoint with user and password to the room so a test order can be sent.
Get the agent to run a smoke test pushing a fake order through the CSV format they use, and confirm the selector user and config are set up.
Delete each test order straight after it is sent to the live TCA endpoint.
Call Pete at 11:30 with the room to show the working CSV flow and agree how to position the API.
Pull the packaging presets from Dispatch Cloud so they can be loaded into the Beachhead demo customer.
Mirror the live templates and packaging presets under the Beachhead demo customer.
Pull together some docs on the carrier proxy mocks so Speaker 1 can plug them in for testing.
Send Speaker 1 a link to the remote dev machine setup, to help with the laptop RAM limits.
Set up automatic SFTP key generation.
Find out whether FedEx needs a commodity block per package for multi-pack shipments, and test multi-packs.

questions: Should Speaker 1 steer the Americans towards the API, or push back hard and say the API is a future solution?
Does FedEx need a commodity block for each package in a multi-pack shipment? Nobody has tested it, including the carrier team.
There is no FedEx test account. The earlier live US account is now with a customer, and the current one is TCA's live account, so how much testing can be done on it?
When will the new OpenAPI spec arrive, and who in the carriers team is designing the API? Chris Cummings is handing it over, and Speaker 1 does not know the details.
How should the mezzanine PDA requirement be handled, given the conflict with offline capability and a Friday deadline?
